correctness.rationale: For every composite k>=4,t>=1 with t(k-1)-1>=2, the originating source proves M simply connected and Fix(phi^a) nonempty exactly for gcd(a,k)>1. Armstrong identifies the coarse orbit fundamental group as C_k modulo its subgroup generated by fixed-point elements; elementary gcd shows order p for prime powers and 1 otherwise, and shows every proper subgroup quotient simply connected. Vanishing of H^1(O_M) and of H^2(M,Z) torsion proves Pic(M) torsion-free. Character descent identifies Pic(M/H)_tors with Hom(H/N_H,C*); the universal coefficient theorem identifies H^2 torsion. Boissière--Camere--Sarti Proposition 3.2 supplies 0->Hom(G,C*)->Cl(Y)->Cl(M)^G->0, yielding Cl(Y)_tors=C_k since Cl(M) is torsion-free. The canonical boundary uses the originating source index-two theorem and the absence of torsion Picard classes. verify.py passed for k=2..240, solely as a finite check of subgroup arithmetic.

value.rationale: The coarse fundamental group, integral degree-two torsion, Picard torsion, and Weil-versus-Cartier torsion are exact natural invariants of the singular cyclic Calabi–Yau quotients, not arbitrary isolated counts. The classification has a nontrivial prime-support phase transition: prime powers retain one prime-order Cartier/topological remnant while mixed-prime orders lose them even though the Weil torsion remains order k. It supplies a complete family-wide answer and explicit infinite simply connected log-Enriques examples with non-Cartier canonical order-two torsion. It does not claim full cohomology or the complete class group.
